title: How to Use IB SEHS Exam Papers in the Final Weeks
summary: Use IB SEHS exam papers in the final weeks to practise timing, apply the markscheme, track errors, and repair weak topics before your final exam with…
body_markdown:
IB SEHS exam papers are most useful when you complete a timed attempt, mark it honestly, record errors, repair weak topics, and test them again. In the final weeks, this cycle turns practice into a revision plan.


Reading about energy systems can feel productive. An exam question asks something more demanding: select the relevant mechanism, apply it to a sporting context, and explain it precisely. Practice reveals which knowledge you can use independently.


Treat each paper as evidence. The score matters, but the reasons behind lost marks tell you what to study next.


### Your final-weeks checklist


- Check that questions match your syllabus and assessment format.
- Use the correct time limit and permitted materials.
- Mark responses against the relevant IB SEHS markscheme.
- Separate knowledge, application, interpretation, and timing errors.
- Repair weak concepts with focused notes and questions.
- Retry difficult questions after 2-3 days without the answers.
- Finish with a realistic timed rehearsal.


### Check that the paper matches your course


The current SEHS course has its first assessment in May 2026. Its external assessment includes Paper 1A multiple-choice questions, Paper 1B data-based and experimental-work questions, and Paper 2 short-answer and extended-response questions. Older resources may contain useful questions, but their coverage and structure may differ.


Compare resources with the syllabus your teacher has provided. The[IB SEHS subject resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-sports-exercise-and-health-science-sehs-new-syllabus) and[complete IB SEHS HL and SL guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ultimate-guide-to-ib-sports-exercise-and-health-science-sehs-hl-and-sl) can help orient your practice.


Keep older questions when their content remains relevant. Avoid treating an outdated paper structure as a template for your examination.


### Begin with one honest timed attempt


Imagine a student who can explain muscle contraction comfortably, then leaves an extended response unfinished under timed conditions. That attempt reveals a problem that rereading alone could miss.


Choose a representative paper and complete it without notes, messages, or mid-paper marking. Follow the official time for your level and session. When stuck, write what you can, flag the question, and continue.


One full attempt can establish your baseline. Between full papers, use the[IB SEHS Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-sports-exercise-and-health-science-sehs-new-syllabus/questionbank) to isolate weaknesses rather than repeatedly answering familiar material.


A student coaches a tiny brain through an unusual revision workout


### Use the IB SEHS markscheme to diagnose mistakes


Compare each mark point with what you actually wrote. Credit requires the relevant idea to appear clearly; an explanation you intended to include cannot earn marks.


Your wording need not match every model sentence. Look for scientific accuracy, relevance, and any accepted alternatives. When uncertain about a valid alternative, ask your teacher.


Check command terms closely. Identifying a factor does not explain its effect. An evaluation needs balanced reasoning and a supported judgement. The[guide to mastering IB SEHS vocabulary](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-master-the-vocabulary-of-ib-sports-science) can help when terminology repeatedly costs marks.


Label lost marks consistently:


- **K:** missing or inaccurate knowledge
- **A:** weak application to the context
- **D:** misread data or experimental information
- **C:** unfulfilled command term
- **T:** incomplete work under time pressure
- **E:** vague scientific expression


A score describes performance. A pattern of application errors identifies tomorrow’s work.


### Build an error log that guides action


Keep the log brief and specific. Copying entire markschemes creates more reading without necessarily changing your next session.


Question or topic Why the mark was lost Repair action Retest date


Cardiovascular drift Effect described without mechanism Review thermoregulation; answer two application questions Thursday


Force-time graph Axes misread Complete three data-based questions Friday


Extended response Final judgement missing Write a conclusion using the evidence Saturday


Choose repairs according to the error. Recall problems call for Study Notes, Flashcards, and focused[IB SEHS self-study resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-ib-sehs-resources-self-study) . Application problems need unfamiliar contexts. Unfocused extended responses need planning practice.


RevisionDojo’s AI Chat can clarify concepts, while grading tools offer additional feedback. Compare that feedback with the markscheme and your teacher’s guidance, particularly when scientific wording is ambiguous.


### Repair weak topics, then retest them


Work on the smallest useful gap. If a question linking lactate threshold and endurance performance caused difficulty, review that concept, explain it from memory, and answer 3-5 related questions. Return to the original question after a delay.


Immediate corrections can feel convincing because the answer remains fresh. A delayed attempt tests whether you can retrieve the explanation independently.


A flexible schedule keeps this process manageable:


- **Around three weeks before:** complete a baseline paper and repair major content gaps. Use the[IB SEHS revision strategies guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revision-strategies-that-work-for-ib-sports-science-exams) to combine recall and question practice.
- **Around two weeks before:** alternate targeted drills with timed sections, mixing topics to practise selecting relevant concepts. Follow the[IB SEHS mock exam preparation guidance](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-sehs-mock-exam-prep-november) for further structure.
- **During the final week:** complete a limited number of full rehearsals and review recurring errors. The[one-week IB SEHS revision guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-cram-ib-sport-science-in-1-week) can help prioritise remaining weaknesses.


Adjust this schedule to your available time. Leave room to review each attempt before starting another.


### Make the final attempt a rehearsal


Clear your desk, prepare permitted equipment, and obey the stopping time. Practise moving on from difficult questions and checking unfinished responses when time remains.


RevisionDojo brings preparation together through its Questionbank, Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat, and grading tools. Predicted Papers and Mock Exams support timed practice in Exam mode; Tutors can help resolve persistent misunderstandings. The Coursework Library serves a separate coursework need, while your final revision sessions should remain focused on exam readiness.


After each rehearsal, choose a concrete next action: repair a mechanism, practise a graph, or plan an evaluation. Progress comes from correcting an error and demonstrating that correction independently on the next attempt.
